headline: Record midstream volumes lift margins, outlook firms
summary_short: Targa Resources reported record Q2 2026 results with revenue up 4.2% y/y to $4.44B and net income attributable to shareholders up 21.5% y/y to $764.6M ($3.54 diluted EPS), as company-labeled adjusted EBITDA rose 38% y/y and 14% q/q to a record $1,603.1M.
summary_long: Growth was driven by record Permian natural gas inlet, NGL transportation, fractionation and LPG export volumes plus higher marketing margin in Logistics & Transportation; G&P adjusted operating margin rose 21% y/y on record Permian inlet volumes despite lower and negative Waha gas prices. Revenue growth (+4.2% y/y) reflected a 36% rise in fee-based midstream-service revenue, largely offsetting flat commodity sales. Cost of product purchases and fuel fell 6% y/y on lower natural gas prices. Targa now expects FY2026 adjusted EBITDA toward the top end of its unchanged $5.7-5.9B range, while holding net growth capex (~$4.5B) and maintenance capex (~$250M) guidance steady. It paid a $1.25/share dividend (+25% y/y) and repurchased $80M of stock; cash was $132.3M against $19.58B long-term debt.

drivers.explanation: Fee-based midstream revenue rose 36% y/y on higher gathering, processing, transportation and fractionation fees and export volumes, mostly offsetting flat commodity sales.
Driven by record Permian natural gas inlet volumes in G&P and higher marketing, pipeline transportation, fractionation and LPG export margin in L&T.
Higher operating income was partly offset by higher interest expense on higher borrowings and higher income tax expense tied to increased pre-tax income.
Decrease reflected lower natural gas prices, partially offset by higher NGL prices and higher NGL and natural gas volumes.
Record quarter on record Permian, NGL transport, fractionation and LPG export volumes; company now expects FY2026 adjusted EBITDA toward the top end of its unchanged $5.7-5.9B range.
